title: Unify task submission and review-claim identity through synchronized lifecycle verbs
description: TASK-266 review and live TASK-267 alignment exposed two SYN-0001 lifecycle seams. Submission exists only as db/claims.py submit_task(), which mutates SQLite but cannot append a SUBMISSION event or sync task/graph mirrors. claim_review() assumes the reviewer already exists in agents, while map_task.py owns registration; the foreign-key failure is flattened into False and misreported as already claimed. Add one sanctioned synchronized submission verb and one explicit review-claim identity contract without broad lifecycle redesign.
acceptance_criteria: map_task.py exposes a sanctioned submit verb that verifies the current claimant, transitions to SUBMITTED, appends a canonical SUBMISSION event, and synchronizes task JSON and graph mirrors.
The documented submission path points agents to the synchronized verb; direct low-level submit_task use is clearly internal or returns enough data for a synchronized caller.

claim_review handles an unregistered valid reviewer through one declared registration contract or returns a distinct diagnosable failure; a foreign-key error cannot collapse into the same False as an occupied review claim.
End-to-end tests reproduce both live failures and prove SQLite, task mirrors, graph, events, reviewer identity, and review-claim state agree after each transition.
TASK-266 completes first so overlapping claims.py/map_task.py output ownership never occurs.
